QF.id: SIA Social Stock Exchange Introduction and Instruments_48

question.text: Under the SEBI ICDR Regulations 2018, the definition of 'For Profit Social Enterprise' specifically EXCLUDES which type of entity?

answer.text: Partnership firms with more than 20 partners.
Limited Liability Partnerships with foreign LPs.
A company incorporated under Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook pp.56-57, the For Profit Social Enterprise definition specifically excludes a company incorporated under Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013. Section 8 companies are described as an NPO form, so excluding them from the FPE definition prevents double-counting across the NPO and FPE categories. The Trap: Options A, B and C each invent unrelated carve-outs (partnership-firm size, LLP foreign-LP, sole proprietorship by location) that do not appear in the workbook. Note: Section 8 companies sit on the NPO side of the bright line; any other for-profit body corporate may qualify as an FPE if it meets the social-enterprise eligibility criteria.
